IOM continued to provide support to the National Coordination Mechanism on Migration (NCM). The support in 2020 included: establishing a fully functional NCM Secretariat at the Office of the Vice President (OVP) with donation of equipment; and operationalizing 6 out of the 8 Thematic Working Groups (TWGs) under the NCM. 

2021:
A high level National Coordination Mechanism (NCM) meeting was led by the Office of the Vice President (OVP) in 17 February 2021 with  35 Government Ministries, agencies, CSOs and UN agencies participating. Presentation of the 2021 NCM workplan was done during the meeting
-	Under the overall guidance of the OVP as the lead for the NCM and technical lead of  Ministry of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Gambians Abroad (MOFA),  the first voluntary national review of the implementation of  Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration (GCM) in The Gambia was done in May 2021. With technical assistance from IOM, the report presents the Government of The Gambia’s progress in the implementation of the GCM following The Gambia’s decision to undertake a national review. This review will contribute to the 2021 Africa Regional Review to serve as an input to the International Migration Review Forum (IMRF) to be conducted in 2022

ILO’s strategy will focus on supporting GCCI in the expansion of its service offer focusing on women entrepreneurship and of its membership to newly formalized entrepreneurs. In order to guarantee sustainability, the strategy will be to build capacity of GCCI staff to deliver these services in a sustainable way using tools developed by the ILO. 
As GCCI will be the implementing partner of the ILO on a project funded by the Italian cooperation (Promotion of formal and innovative entrepreneurship in Senegal and The Gambia), synergies will be developed with the project. The project will indeed allow the ILO to develop an arsenal of tools for the formalization of informal enterprises. GCCI will channel these tools to existing and potential members increasing thus its offer of business development and referral services. The GCCI will build on these initiatives to expand its membership to newly formalized entrepreneurs Considering the prevailing Covid-19 outbreak, the ILO will support GCCI in providing information and training services that respond to its members’needs.

projects.name: TRAINING WORKSHOP FOR FRONT LINE OFFICIALS ON THE STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR HANDLING SMUGGLING OF MIGRANTS CASES IN THE GAMBIA
projects.description:
The training workshop aims to build the capacity of all frontline officials on the elements of the crime of smuggling of migrants, related offences, and to have a first-hand understanding of how to apply to SOP in handling SOM cases from a human rights based gender responsive and child sensitive approach. Furthermore, the workshop is expected to enhance the capability and skills of front line personnel to identify and properly protect migrants in vulnerable situations including migrants who have been object of smuggling. Given the diversity of front line officials targeting for this activity, the workshop will provide a clear overview of the coordination mechanism between stakeholders in not only providing assistance and support to migrants in vulnerable situations, but coordination, collaboration and communication when it comes to investigating and prosecuting crimes relating to migrant smuggling in the absence of a law criminalizing smuggling of migrants in the Gambia. 

In view of the above, the main objectives of this activity are to:

•	Train front line officials to have a good knowledge of basic concepts pertaining to human trafficking and migrant smuggling and to understanding the constituent elements of these crimes.
•	Train front line officials to detect potential victims of trafficking and smuggled migrants and refer them to national authorities accordingly.
•	Strengthen the comprehension of front line officials on human rights in the context of migration – in particular at international borders while integrating a human rights, gender responsive and child sensitive approach to handling migrant smuggling cases
•	Provide a practical understanding of applying the National Referral Mechanism in protecting and assisting vulnerable migrants including victims of human trafficking.
•	Provide a practical understanding of the application of the draft Standard Operation Procedure to manage smuggling cases and to successfully identify and refer migrants in vulnerable situations.
•	Enhance the understanding of frontline officials of potential human rights protection needs of smuggled migrants.

projects.name: International Day against Human Trafficking - Blue Heart Campaign
projects.description:
The "Blue Heart" campaign is an initiative designed to mobilise public opinion in the fight against human trafficking and its impact on society. The blue heart symbolises the despair of the victims of trafficking and reminds us of the cruelty of those who buy, sell or exploit other human beings. Further information: https://www.unodc.org/blueheart/fr/about-us.html.

GENERAL OBJECTIVE

Raising awareness and mobilising the public and decision-makers on human trafficking.


SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES
- Mobilising public opinion and decision-makers to combat human trafficking and its consequences for society.
 	
- The aim of the Blue Heart campaign is to encourage everyone to get involved and support the fight against this crime.
 	
It also enables everyone to show their support for the victims of trafficking by "wearing" a Blue Heart or displaying a Blue Heart on various media (paper or online).

During this commemoration, the Gambia proudly launched the Blue Heart Campaign and joined other countries in supporting Victims of trafficking.

projects.name: PROTECTING THE DIGNITY AND RIGHTS OF MIGRANTS IN VULNERABLE SITUATIONS WITH GENDER AND CHILD CONSIDERATIONS: Trafficking in Persons and Smuggling of Migrants
projects.description:
The training workshop aims to build the capacity of Staff and Volunteer of the GRCS on the elements of the crime of smuggling of migrants and related offences as well as trafficking in persons. Furthermore, the workshop is expected to enhance their capability and skills to identify and adequately support victims of trafficking and other migrants in vulnerable situations.  Likewise, the activity intends to strengthen their capacity to adopt a pragmatic human rights-based, gender-responsive and child sensitive approach in responding to trafficking in persons and migrant smuggling cases.
In view of the above, the main objectives of this activity are to:
1.	Train GRCS volunteers and staff to have a good knowledge of basic concepts pertaining to human trafficking and migrant smuggling and to understanding the constituent elements of these crimes.
2.	Equip GRCS volunteers and staff as frontline practitioners and caseworkers with the skills necessary to recognize the signs of trafficking; identify the constitutive elements of the crime and provide tailored support or referral.
3.	Provide a practical understanding of applying the National Referral Mechanism in protecting and assisting and referring migrants in vulnerable situations including victims of human trafficking and migrants that are fleeing prosecution and are in need of international protection
4.	Recognize the specific vulnerability of migrant children, particularly those in irregular situations, and to ensure that they respond to children’s specific needs that reflect the best interests of each child.
5.	Empower the GRCS with the knowledge to adopt a gender sensitive approach when providing support and assistance to vulnerable migrants particularly women and girls who may have faced trauma as a result of violence and other human rights violations.
6.	Train GRCS volunteers and staff to adopt a victim’s rights-centred and victim-friendly approach in assisting and protecting trafficked persons and migrants in vulnerable situations.
7.	Provide a practical understanding of the application of the validated Standard Operating Procedure to manage smuggling cases and refer vulnerable migrants.
8.	Provide participants with a detailed overview of the Human Rights Principles and Guidelines of migrants in vulnerable situations.

projects.name: TRAINING WORKSHOP FOR FRONT LINE OFFICIALS ON THE STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE FOR HANDLING SMUGGLING OF MIGRANTS CASES IN THE GAMBIA
projects.description:
The training workshop aims to build the capacity of all frontline officials on the elements of the crime of smuggling of migrants, related offences, and to have a first-hand understanding of how to apply to SOP in handling SOM cases from a human rights based gender responsive and child sensitive approach. Furthermore, the workshop is expected to enhance the capability and skills of front line personnel to identify and properly protect migrants in vulnerable situations including migrants who have been object of smuggling. Given the diversity of front line officials targeting for this activity, the workshop will provide a clear overview of the coordination mechanism between stakeholders in not only providing assistance and support to migrants in vulnerable situations, but coordination, collaboration and communication when it comes to investigating and prosecuting crimes relating to migrant smuggling in the absence of a law criminalizing smuggling of migrants in the Gambia. This particular training is targeted in senior officials to ensure the effective implementation and application of the SOP across the country.

In view of the above, the main objectives of this activity are to:

•	Train front line officials to have a good knowledge of basic concepts pertaining to human trafficking and migrant smuggling and to understanding the constituent elements of these crimes.
•	Train front line officials to detect potential victims of trafficking and smuggled migrants and refer them to national authorities accordingly.
•	Strengthen the comprehension of front line officials on human rights in the context of migration – in particular at international borders while integrating a human rights, gender responsive and child sensitive approach to handling migrant smuggling cases
•	Provide a practical understanding of applying the National Referral Mechanism in protecting and assisting vulnerable migrants including victims of human trafficking.
•	Provide a practical understanding of the application of the draft Standard Operation Procedure to manage smuggling cases and to successfully identify and refer migrants in vulnerable situations.
•	Enhance the understanding of frontline officials of potential human rights protection needs of smuggled migrants.
